voices.name: A robot
voices.teaches: What phrasing does, by taking it away. Read it again as yourself straight after and the difference is the lesson.

voices.name: A whisper
voices.how: Quiet enough that somebody across the room leans in.
voices.teaches: Phrasing without volume. A whisper that still groups its words proves the phrasing is real and not just loudness.

voices.name: A sports announcer
voices.how: Loud and fast, like the last ten seconds of a game.
voices.teaches: Pace, and the nerve to push it. Speed collapses into mumbling unless the phrases hold.

voices.name: Telling a secret
voices.how: Like you are telling one person something nobody else should hear.
voices.teaches: Leaning on the words that matter. A secret has to land, so the stress goes somewhere on purpose.

voices.name: Just woke up
voices.how: Slow and heavy, one eye still shut.
voices.teaches: Holding a phrase together when it is slow. Slow is where word-by-word reading hides.

voices.name: Very excited
voices.how: Like you just found out something brilliant.
voices.teaches: Pitch moving across a sentence instead of sitting flat.

voices.name: A newsreader
voices.how: Clear and even. This is the six o'clock news.
voices.teaches: The neutral expert read. This one is the target, which is why it comes after the silly ones.

voices.name: Grumpy
voices.how: Like somebody made you read it.
voices.teaches: That tone is a choice. The words did not change; the feeling did.

voices.name: A giant
voices.how: Low and enormous. The floor shakes.
voices.teaches: Breath and volume across a whole phrase rather than one word at a time.

voices.name: A tiny mouse
voices.teaches: Speed and clarity together. Fast and tiny still has to be understood.

voices.name: A bit scared
voices.how: Like something is behind the door.
voices.teaches: Pausing for meaning. Fear puts the breaks in different places, and the child chooses where.

voices.name: Completely bored
voices.how: Like this is the dullest sentence ever written.
voices.teaches: The opposite of expression, named out loud. Children recognise this voice, which is why it is worth making fun of.

punctuation.name: Telling
punctuation.how: Your voice goes down at the end. You are stating it.

punctuation.name: Asking
punctuation.how: Your voice goes up at the end. You want an answer.

punctuation.name: Meaning it
punctuation.how: Louder and sharper. You are surprised, or you are certain.
